subject: Hosted API committed uplift — staggered increase & fallback lanes
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena@marketflux.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@marketflux.com
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — request for staggered commit increase and fallback lanes

Hi Hannah,

Renewal for MarketFlux (deal MF-2028-1624) hits in mid-September. We ran the Q2 stress tests and expect a sustained 55% month-over-month growth in hosted API calls starting Oct — with a big seasonal spike in November. We want to: 1) increase the monthly committed tokens across three months (Oct/Nov/Dec) instead of a single immediate uplift, and 2) keep a clear, low-latency fallback policy if a rate band is hit.

Can Redwood provide a staggered commit schedule and confirm the soft-fallback behavior (auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant vs queueing)? Attached is our usage forecast. If you can send an amendment draft and a quick ops checklist, we can move procurement quickly.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Platform, MarketFlux
--
Attachment: marketflux_usage_forecast_q4.csv (spreadsheet, 72KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@marketflux.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — request for staggered commit increase and fallback lanes

Elena,

Thanks for the forecast — this is helpful and aligns with patterns we've seen on similar retail/marketplace accounts. High level: we can support a three-step commit ladder (Oct: +40%, Nov: +80%, Dec: +100%) with pre-agreed burst pockets and an automated model-fallback policy. Key notes:
- Staggered commits will be billed at the committed rate per month; any burst beyond committed + burst pocket will be billed at overage rates (see attached rateband matrix).
- Fallback behavior: primary routing will attempt the pinned high-capacity model; if capacity constraints occur we automatically route to a compatible lower-cost model variant for read-heavy requests and preserve latency SLOs for priority routes.

I've attached a proposed amendment (v3) with the commit ladder and fallback language. Next steps:
1) Vanessa will confirm pricing and the exact burst pocket sizing.
2) Kar thik will confirm contract language for automatic fallback and SLA exceptions.
3) If procurement signs off, we can provide a DocuSign link for an addendum.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk the ops plan.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: redwood_proposed_amendment_v3.pdf (PDF, 45 pages)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@marketflux.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal coming up — request for staggered commit increase and fallback lanes

Elena — looping in Marcus from Pricing & Platform Ops to confirm numbers. Quick pricing summary (proposed):
- Oct commit: 40% increase over current monthly commit — billed at current committed rate.
- Nov commit: additional 40% (total +80%) — step discount applied on incremental tokens (see rateband).
- Dec commit: total +100% with a seasonal uplift discount for the month (one-off credit if usage exceeds forecast).
- Burst pockets: we recommend a 15% monthly burst pocket for Oct/Nov and a 25% pocket for Dec.

We'll include a granular rateband matrix in the amendment and flag which API routes qualify for priority routing (to guarantee latency SLOs during fallback). Marcus, can you confirm the exact numbers in the Excel and whether a minor pro-rata for Oct is required?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Growth — Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: rateband_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 8KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 1 Sep 2028 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — request for staggered commit increase and fallback lanes

All,

Reviewed the amendment text in v3. A couple of legal/ops clarifications we should lock before routing to procurement:
1) "Fallback routing" — specify which routes are eligible (we recommend: inference/generation, embeddings read-only routes excluded unless MarketFlux opts in).
2) SLA exception window — define a monthly aggregate threshold (e.g., >95th percentile token rate sustained for 3 minutes) that triggers automatic fallback to avoid noisy short bursts causing tier changes.
3) Pro-rata for Oct: because the ladder starts mid-billing cycle, we propose a daily pro-rata calculation on Oct's commit uplift; include an option for MarketFlux to front-load the Oct uplift for predictable billing.

If MarketFlux is ok with the above, we can update the amendment and send to procurement + DocuSign.

-Karthik
Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference

If we can get the DocuSign this week, we can finalize before the mid-September renewal deadline.

Best,
